steps.title: Tell Us About Your Windows
steps.brief: How to get in touch and what is useful to send first (which rooms, roughly how many windows, what they want the blind or curtain to do: darker, more private, cooler, warmer; photos if they have them). No promise of a reply time unless [CV: response_time] is set.

steps.title: We Measure and Price the Job
steps.brief: The visit and what gets measured and looked at (the recess and its depth, the handles and the sill, which way the window opens, what is behind the plaster where the brackets will go, the room and when the sun reaches it). Follows [CV: quote_method]; only say the quote is written if quote_method says so. Never restates 'free' (FAQ 5 owns it); samples brought to the house or a showroom only where [CV: quote_method] or the confirmed practices say so.

steps.title: We Fit on a Date That Suits You
steps.brief: The fitting date is agreed in advance, to suit the customer, once what was ordered has been made (the making stage in the trade facts). The time between the measure and the fitting only from [CV: start_time]: the trade facts give no lead time for any blind, curtain, shutter or awning, so never a number of days or weeks. Never mention the price, the quote or changes to the order (step 2 and Why choose us own them). Never restates the start time (FAQ 4 owns it).

step_2_no_visit.title: We Price Your Job
step_2_no_visit.brief: Say a price is agreed before any work starts. Describe how the price is reached only from [CV: quote_method]; when quote_method is blank, name no method at all (no photos, call, video, measurements sent in or visit). Only say the quote is written if quote_method says so. Never restates 'free' (FAQ 5 owns it).

faq_slots.question: Do you guarantee your work?

A maker's warranty on a motor, a mechanism or a fabric is described as the maker's, from [CV: manufacturer_warranty] only; never a fitting guarantee the client values do not give.

faq_slots.question: What happens if something isn't right after the fitting?

Then the 'reasonable care and skill' standard every trade works to, as the standard the work is held to, never as a defence. No promise to come back or put it right for free. Never invent a guarantee. Never say a made to measure order has no comeback: the trade facts say a fault keeps its rights whoever measured, and say nothing about who pays for a wrong measurement.

faq_slots.question: How soon can you fit them?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: start_time] only, as given, as the time from the order or the measure to the fitting. The trade facts give no lead time for any blind, curtain, shutter or awning (Table G), so never a number of days or weeks that is not in the client values. Code adds "bigger projects are booked further ahead" only when that practice is confirmed.

faq_slots.question: Is the quote free and no obligation?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [QUOTE_FREE] and [CV: quote_method]. A measuring visit is called free only when [QUOTE_FREE] says so.

faq_slots.question: How do your quotes work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] only.

faq_slots.question: How long does it take from measuring to fitting?
faq_slots.answer_brief: What decides it, with no number: the blind, curtain or shutter is made to the measurements after the order (the making stage in the trade facts), so the maker's time, the number of windows and whether a motor or a bent track is involved set the gap. A figure only from [CV: start_time]. The fitting itself runs all year indoors; an awning waits for suitable weather (the trade facts timing cells).

faq_slots.question: Why is there still light coming in around my blackout blind?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different causes in plain words: the gap a blind inside the recess needs at each side to run, a blind made narrower than the window, light over the top of the roll or under a curtain that stops at the sill. Then what the local housing adds (a deep recess on a sash window, a shallow reveal on a uPVC window), then the fix from the trade facts fact rows: a blind on the wall across the recess reaching past the frame, side channels, a blind framed to the glass, lined curtains. Say what it reduces; never total darkness (the fact row: a blackout fabric does not decide what happens at the edges).

faq_slots.question: Will my blind sit in the recess or on the wall?
faq_slots.answer_brief: What decides it, from the trade facts stages: the depth of the recess against the handles, tiles or a sill that stands proud. A shallow recess, or a room where the dark matters, sends the blind onto the wall across the recess, covering some wall either side of the frame. A blind framed to the glass is the third choice on a uPVC window: it is held by clips at the beading, so nothing is screwed into the frame. What the brackets go into decides the fixing (plasterboard, a steel or concrete lintel, uPVC), checked for hidden cables and pipes first. Never a figure.

faq_slots.question: What makes a blind child safe?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Calm, and as what usually applies, from the trade facts rule and fact rows: a new blind with a looped cord or chain is sold with a part that holds the loop taut or lets it separate under a pull, and the fitter screws that part to the wall high enough to be out of a small child's reach; a blind made with no cord needs none. This holds in every home, not only where children live. The fitter leaves the warning labels on and shows how the part works. An older blind can have one added. Never a standard's number, never the height as a measurement, never a scare, never blame, never 'completely safe'.

faq_slots.question: Will an awning or outside shutters need planning permission?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Point at the trade facts rule rows (Table C) and write what usually applies, with "usually" or "in most cases": an awning on a house is often allowed without an application but not always; a listed home, a conservation area, a flat, or an awning that reaches out over the pavement is where a consent or a licence can come in; a shop's name on the fabric can need its own consent; blinds, curtains and inside shutters need none. What the customer does about it only as the row gives it (check with the council, apply where it is needed). Never an Act's or an order's name, never a size or a height.

cards.title: Sun in the room at the wrong time of day
cards.brief: A situation card, not a fault: a bedroom light long before anyone wants to wake, a child's room still bright at bedtime in June, glare across the television or a screen in the afternoon, a conservatory or a south facing room too warm to sit in while the sun is on it, and the same glass letting the warmth out on a winter night. What decides it: the glass, with nothing at it to check the sun or hold the warmth, and the hour the sun reaches that window. What the work gives them, said as what it reduces or blocks and never as a temperature or a dark room promised: a blind fitted on the wall across the recess so the light cannot get round the sides, a lined or blackout lined curtain, slats or louvres that tilt the glare away, a roof blind with a reflective backing against the summer heat, a closed blind, shutter or lined curtain that cuts the heat lost through the glass (the trade facts fact row: through the glass, never a saving on a bill, never a figure). By category: Blind Shop reads it as the blind and its fit; Curtain Shop as the lining and where the pole or track ends; Curtain Fitter as the track or pole and how much wall it covers either side of the frame. Never a lifestyle pitch, never a fault invented for it.
cards.mechanism: the glass, with nothing at it to check the sun or hold the warmth

cards.title: Overlooked from the street or next door
cards.brief: A situation card: a front room a step from the pavement, a bathroom window facing the neighbour's landing, a kitchen the whole garden looks into, a bedroom lit from inside at night. What decides it: a window in full view with nothing adjustable at it, so the choice is a bare window or a closed one, and whether the customer wants privacy by day with the daylight kept, or privacy at night with the room lit. What the work gives them, in plain words from the trade facts materials cells: slats or louvres that tilt so the room keeps its light and loses the view in (Venetian and wooden blinds, shutters, vertical blinds); a day and night roller; a voile behind the curtains for the day and lined curtains for the evening. By category: Blind Shop reads it as the tilt and the fabric; Curtain Shop as the voile and the lining; Curtain Fitter as a second track or pole so a voile and a curtain hang together. Never what is in anyone's window today, never a judgement on the street, never 'complete privacy'.
cards.mechanism: a window in full view with nothing adjustable at it

cards.title: A window nothing off the shelf will fit
cards.brief: Window led: the situation the window causes, never a fault in the house. A bay with three or five faces, a tilt and turn window whose handle swings into the recess, a shallow reveal with no depth for a blind, a sash window with a deep recess, a roof window over a bed, a conservatory with sloping or shaped panes, a tall window on a stairwell. What decides it: the window's shape, depth and handles, which decide where anything can sit and what it can be fixed to. What the work gives them, from the trade facts stages: a blind measured for that recess with room for the handles, or fitted on the wall across it; a blind framed to the glass and clipped to the beading of a uPVC window with no drilling into the frame; a track bent to the shape of the bay so the curtains run round in one, or a blind to each face; a roof window blind chosen by the window's make and size code; shaped blinds measured pane by pane for a conservatory. By category: Blind Shop reads it as the blind and the fixing; Curtain Fitter as the bent track and its brackets; Curtain Shop as the curtains made to the bay's drop and width. Never a brand name for the system.
cards.mechanism: the window's shape, depth and handles

cards.title: Blinds and curtains that no longer do their job
cards.brief: Problem led: a roller that drops back down or will not raise, a snapped chain, slats that will not tilt, a pole that droops in the middle, a track pulling away from the wall, hems that drag on the carpet or stop short, a lining gone thin while the fabric is still good, a cord or chain hanging in a loop in a home that now has small children. The one cause this card makes: a worn part, or a fixing that was never right for what is behind the plaster. Say what the fix usually involves, from the trade facts stages: the part matched and replaced (parts for a known make; a blind of an unknown make may not have one), the brackets refixed into whatever is actually there (plasterboard, a steel or concrete lintel, a uPVC frame where its terms allow it), curtains shortened or relined, a device added to an older blind and its warning labels left on. Honest that a repair or an alteration is often the better answer; never a dig at who fitted it, never 'past saving' as a sale. Child safety calm and as what usually applies, never a scare. By category: Blind Shop reads it as repairs and child safe blinds; Curtain Fitter as alterations, tracks and poles; Curtain Shop as relining and alterations.
cards.mechanism: a worn part, or a fixing that was never right for the wall

cost.h2: What Affects the Cost of [WORK] in [CITY]

cards.title: How many windows, and how big
cards.brief: The number of windows and their size move the price more than anything else: more fabric or more slats, a wider roller or a longer track, more brackets, more time at each one (the trade facts price rows). Say it plainly and give no figure.

cards.title: The shape of the window
cards.brief: A bay with its faces, a sloping or shaped pane in a conservatory, a roof window, a curved track: each takes more measuring, a track curved to the bay or a blind per face, and longer to fit than a flat window (the price rows). Say why the shape adds work, without a figure.

cards.title: What the brackets go into, and how high
cards.brief: Plasterboard over a steel lintel, a concrete lintel, a uPVC frame, old plaster that crumbles: each needs its own fixing, and the wall is checked for hidden cables and pipes before anything is drilled (the trade facts stages and fact rows). A stairwell window, a conservatory roof or a roof window adds safe access and time. Say the business looks before it prices, from [CV: quote_method] only. No figure.

cards.title: How it works and what it's made of
cards.brief: A chain against a motor (battery, mains or solar), side channels or a cassette on a roller, a lined, blackout lined or interlined curtain against an unlined one, wood against aluminium slats, a bent track against a straight pole, from the trade facts materials cells and price rows. Name a material or a system only if the trade facts or [CV: materials_methods] give it; a named product only from [CV: materials_methods]. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.

faq_slots.question: How much does [WORK_LOWER] cost in [CITY]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Prices only from [CV: price_list]; otherwise the three things that move the price for this kind of work (the number and size of the windows, their shape, how the blind or curtain is operated and lined) and how the quote is given, from [CV: quote_method] only.

faq_slots.question: Do you guarantee your [WORK_LOWER] work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Start with yes, then the terms from [CV: guarantee_years] and [CV: guarantee_scope]. A maker's warranty on a motor or a mechanism is the maker's, from [CV: manufacturer_warranty] only. Described, never promised.

faq_slots.question: Are you insured for [WORK_LOWER] work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for. Never what it pays or who it covers.

faq_slots.question: What happens if something isn't right after the fitting?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the customer does: tell us and we look at it. Then the reasonable care and skill standard every trade works to. No promise to come back free. Never invent a guarantee. Never say a made to measure order has no comeback: the trade facts say a fault keeps its rights whoever measured.

faq_slots.question: What does your [WORK_LOWER] work include?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The jobs themselves, named from the card list (the kinds of blind, curtain, track, shutter or repair the business does), and the size of job taken on, from the services list and [CV: typical_jobs] only. Link one service page. Never 'on this page', 'listed above' or 'the card list' as words: the reader sees no list, so name the work. Measuring is a stage of the job in the trade facts and may be named as one; a free visit only from [QUOTE_FREE].

faq_slots.question: What happens when I ask for a quote?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] and the confirmed practices only: what the customer sends, what the business measures and looks at, what comes back. No timescale unless [CV: response_time] is set. Samples, a showroom or a home visit only where quote_method or the practices say so.

faq_slots.question: How long does [WORK_LOWER] take from measuring to fitting?
faq_slots.answer_brief: What decides it, from the trade facts timing cells and with no number: the order is made to the measurements before it is fitted, so the maker's time, the number of windows and anything bent, shaped or motorised set the gap; the fitting itself is usually done in one visit for a home's worth of windows only where [CV: typical_jobs] says so. A figure only from [CV: start_time]. Indoor fitting runs all year; nothing about a busy season or booking ahead.

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked. Where the symptom follows the sun or the season (a conservatory hot from late spring, low winter sun across a screen, a bedroom light at dawn in June), say first that the sun on that glass at that hour is doing what it does, then what is not usual. Then the usual cause in the window or the fitting, in plain words, what the local housing adds (how the houses were built and the windows they were built with, never the state of the reader's windows), and what the business does about it. One figure at most.

items.title: Measuring the window
items.brief: The survey and measure stage from the trade facts: the recess and its depth, the handles, the sill and the tiles, which way the window opens, where the sun comes from. A part of the job, not a promise about the quote or a free visit.

items.title: Choosing the fit and the controls
items.brief: In the recess or on the wall across it, which side the control hangs, chain, cordless or motor, the lining and the heading for a curtain: from the trade facts materials and methods cell or [CV: materials_methods]. A named product only from [CV: materials_methods].

items.title: Checking what the brackets go into
items.brief: The fixing stage from the trade facts: what is behind the plaster (plasterboard, a steel or concrete lintel, uPVC, timber), the fixings chosen for it, and the wall checked for hidden cables and pipes before any drilling. Never a drill or a fixing named as a brand.

items.title: Making it to your measurements
items.brief: The making stage from the trade facts: the blind, curtain, shutter or awning made to the measurements taken. No lead time: the rows give none, and a figure comes only from [CV: start_time].

items.title: Fitting the brackets level
items.brief: The bracket stage from the trade facts: positions marked clear of the mechanism, brackets fixed and levelled, extra supports where the width or the weight asks for them. No figure.

items.title: Hanging and setting up
items.brief: The central stage from the trade facts: the roller dropped in, the track or pole up and the curtains hung and dressed, the panels hung and aligned, the motor's travel limits set and the remote or hub paired, named as the trade names it.

items.title: Safety devices, and showing you how it works
items.brief: The last stages from the trade facts: any cord or chain device fixed in place, the warning labels left on, the blind or curtain run through its travel and the customer shown how it works. Child safety as what usually applies, calm, never a standard's number.

items.title: Clearing up and the old ones
items.brief: Packaging cleared and the room left as it was found. Old blinds or curtains taken away only from the confirmed practices (waste_removal); otherwise say who takes them away is agreed beforehand (the trade facts rule row).

included.note: Fallback only: the tick items are the service's own Table A stages when the pack gives 6 or more; this set is used when it gives fewer (F-ITEMS-GENERIC).

cards.title: What you notice first
cards.brief: The things a homeowner notices first, from the trade facts signs row, in their words: a roller that drops back down, a chain that has snapped, slats that will not tilt, a curtain that sticks on the bend of a bay, a glider missing, a hem that has dropped, a chain hanging in a loop. The one cause this card makes: a part worn, or a fit that was never right for the window. Then what it leads to if left, from the skipped row: specific, never alarming (a blind that catches on one side wears its fabric at the edge; a loop left hanging stays within reach). On a window led page (Conservatory blinds, Roof window and skylight blinds, Bay window curtains and blinds) the card is the situation the glass or the shape creates, never a fault in the house: heat under a glass roof by early afternoon, light from overhead in a bedroom, glare the sun throws across the room, gaps at the corners of a bay, with the reason in the sun or the shape. On the Child safe blinds page the card is what usually applies to a new blind, said calmly, and the older blind that can have a device added.
cards.mechanism: a part worn, or a fit that was never right for the window

cards.title: Fixings that have let go
cards.brief: A pole that droops, a track pulling away from the wall, a bracket loose, a frame that comes away from the glass, a cord device that has pulled out of the plaster, from the trade facts signs row. The one cause this card makes: a fixing chosen for a different wall from the one it went into (a plasterboard fixing in a steel lintel, a short screw in old plaster, a loaded track on too few supports). Say what the job does underneath so it stays put, from the trade facts stages and the done badly row: find out what is behind the plaster, check for hidden cables and pipes, fix into it with the fixing made for it, add supports where the weight asks for them. No depth or screw size the rows do not give; never a dig at who fitted it. On a window led page: what holds a blind on a sloping pane or a roof window (brackets made for that window, or the make and size code that finds them), and the weight of a bay's curtains on the bends of its track. On the Child safe blinds page: the device fixed firmly and up out of a small child's reach, as what usually applies, never the measurement.
cards.mechanism: a fixing chosen for a different wall from the one it went into

cards.title: Gaps where the light gets through
cards.brief: Light at the sides of a blind, over the top of the roll or under a curtain that stops at the sill; curtains too narrow to meet; light between the sections of a bay; one shaped pane of a conservatory left bare; light round a roof window blind with no side rails, from the trade facts signs rows. The one cause this card makes: a covering narrower, shorter or looser than the window it is on. Say what the job does about it from the stages and fact rows: measured again for that window, fitted on the wall across the recess so it reaches past the frame, side channels or side rails, a lining or an interlining, curtains made to the full width with room to overlap, each face of a bay measured on its own. Say what it reduces; never total darkness (the fact row: the fabric does not decide what happens at the edges). On the Child safe blinds and Blind repairs pages the card reads as the gap a cut down or badly fitting older blind leaves, and that measuring for a new one is where the fix starts. Not a fixing that has let go: card 2 owns that.
cards.mechanism: a covering narrower, shorter or looser than the window it is on

cards.title: Repair it, make it safer, or replace it
cards.brief: The customer's question on every problem led page: whether what they have is worth keeping. The one cause this card makes: wear or age past the point a part can be matched. From the trade facts stages and fact rows: a part is matched to the make and replaced where one exists (parts availability decides what can be done; a part of an unknown make may have no match); a fabric still good is relined, shortened or rehung rather than replaced; an older corded blind has a device added, or is replaced with one made with no cord, as what usually applies, with the warning labels left on; a repair that touches the controls refits the safety devices. Honest that a repair or an alteration is often the better answer, and plain about when it is not (a frame distorted, a fabric frayed from running unevenly, a part no longer made). Never a scare, never blame, never a standard's number, never 'completely safe', never a dig at another trade. On a window led page: an old flat blind under a sloping pane, or a blind cut down for a roof window, against one made for that glass. Not a fixing (card 2) and not a gap (card 3).
cards.mechanism: wear or age past the point a part can be matched

faq_slots.question: Do I need permission for [SERVICE_LOWER]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts rule rows only, put as the thing that usually applies, with "usually" or "in most cases": fitting a blind, a curtain or an inside shutter in a home needs none; an awning or an outside shutter is where a rule can come in (a listed home, a conservation area, a flat, an awning reaching over the pavement, a shop's name on the fabric), and the customer checks with the council and applies where it is needed; a motor wired into the mains is electrical work that in some cases has to be done by a registered electrician or notified, while a plug in or battery motor is not; on the Commercial blinds page, the fabric's fire performance follows the building's own fire risk assessment, never one rule for every building. Never a standard's number, an Act's name or legal advice. Where the rows give no rule, say no permission is usually needed for this work at a home and leave it there.

faq_slots.question: What does your [SERVICE_LOWER] service include?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The What's Included items said as a sentence, in other words: the measuring, the making, the fixing and the setting up. What it does not cover only from the services list, with one sibling service page or the category page linked. Taking the old ones away only from the confirmed practices (waste_removal).

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked. Where the symptom follows the sun or the season (a conservatory hot from late spring, low winter sun across a screen, a bedroom light at dawn in June), say first that the sun on that glass at that hour is doing what it does, then what is not usual. Then the usual cause in the window or the fitting, in plain words, what the local housing adds (the windows the houses were built with, never the state of the reader's), and what this service does about it. One figure at most.

cards.title: The room, and what you need the window to do
cards.brief: The customer's situation: a bedroom slept in past dawn, a child's room at bedtime in summer, a living room with the television against the light, a kitchen or bathroom with steam and splashes, a home office with a screen, a north facing room that loses its warmth through the glass at night, a patio too hot to sit on at midday (Awnings), a shop or office with glare across the screens (Commercial blinds). What decides it: the light, the privacy, the heat and the damp at that window, and the hour the sun reaches it. What the work gives them, from the trade facts materials cell for this service, said as what it reduces or blocks: a blackout lined curtain or a blind on the wall across the recess for the dark, slats that tilt for privacy with daylight kept, a wipeable slat or a fabric made for a wet room, a reflective backing against the heat, a closed blind, shutter or lined curtain that cuts the heat lost through the glass (through the glass, never a bill, never a figure), an awning that shades the patio and comes in when the wind gets up. Never a temperature, never total darkness, never a look sold, never a fault invented for it: the room and its use, not the showroom.
cards.mechanism: what the room is used for, and when the sun reaches it

cards.title: The part you can't judge from the sofa
cards.brief: The customer's situation: they have priced a ready made blind or an online made to measure one and want to know what a fitter who measures adds. What decides it: the measuring and the fixing, which the customer cannot judge once the fabric is up: whether the blind sits in the recess or on the wall across it; how much wall it covers either side of the frame; the clearance the handles need to turn and the window to open; how much of the glass a raised blind or an open pair of curtains still covers; what is behind the plaster where each bracket goes, and the wall checked for hidden cables before the drill touches it, from the trade facts stages for this service. What the work gives them: those decisions made at the window by the person who will fit it, so the thing works in that room. One specific from the stages for this service; never a dig at the online seller or at another trade; no figure the rows do not give.
cards.mechanism: the measuring and the fixing, which decide whether it works

cards.title: Which option suits the window
cards.brief: The customer's situation: they are weighing two or three ways of doing it (a roller against a Roman, wood against aluminium slats, a blind framed to the glass against one on the wall, a chain against a cordless spring or a motor, a battery motor against a mains one, a pole against a track, a track bent round the bay against a blind to each face, shutters against blinds for a street facing room, a lined curtain against a blackout lined one, a cassette awning against an open one). What decides it: the window's shape, depth and handles, the room's use, and how much looking after they want, from the trade facts materials and methods cell for this service (a framed blind only where the beading is deep enough; a mains motor only where the wiring can be run, and new wiring as electrical work in its own right; an awning rated for the wind it will meet). What the work gives them: the option that suits their window, never the one that is best in general. A named product or brand only from [CV: materials_methods]. No claim about lifespan, lead time or cost unless the rows or the client values give it.
cards.mechanism: the window's shape, depth and handles deciding the option

cards.title: What it will need from you afterwards
cards.brief: The customer's situation: they want to know what they are taking on once it is up. What decides it: what the covering needs to keep working, from the trade facts stages and fact rows for this service (slats and fabrics dusted or brush vacuumed and cleaned as the care instructions supplied with them say, never washed on a guess; a battery motor's power kept up as its maker says; a cord or chain device left fixed where it was put and the warning labels left on; an awning brought in when the wind gets up or the rain sets in, and never put away wet; a fabric with a fire finish cleaned only as its own instructions allow, on a commercial page). What the work gives them: an honest picture of what it saves them and what it does not. Never a promise about how it will look or last, never a lifespan; a repair visit offered only where the services list has the page.
cards.mechanism: what the covering needs to keep working

cards.title: Windows set by when the houses were built
cards.brief: Bays that a straight pole will not go round, sash windows with deep recesses, uPVC windows with shallow reveals, tall windows on a landing. The one cause this card makes: the windows the town's houses were built with, which the town profile dates. Say what each era means for the work and nothing about its state. The older terraces and semis, from Victorian to interwar, have their bays: a curved track that follows the angles, or one blind to each face. Period terraces have sash windows with deep recesses: a blind inside the recess with room for the catch. Homes put up or extended in the 1980s and 1990s have uPVC frames: a blind framed to the glass that clips to the beading, so nothing is screwed into the frame. New estates have plasterboard reveals over steel lintels: the fixing chosen for what is actually there, and the wall checked for cables first. Converted mills and Georgian townhouses have tall windows: heavier curtains, more supports, safe access. Said as how the houses were built, never as the state of anyone's windows today, never that a street's windows are draughty, dated or due for replacement (the pack's section 3). Not a worn part or a loose fixing as faults: the town's category and service pages own those.
cards.mechanism: the windows the town's houses were built with

cards.title: Front windows a step from the pavement
cards.brief: Living rooms that passers by look straight into by day, and that light up like a stage at night. The one cause this card makes: a front window on the pavement with nothing adjustable at it; the town profile says which streets are terraced or fronted straight onto the road. What the work gives in plain words, from the trade facts materials cells: slats or louvres that tilt so the room keeps its daylight and loses the view in, a day and night roller, a voile for the day with lined curtains for the evening; where the profile gives blocks of flats whose lease asks for one look from outside, a plain backing the street sees. Where the profile gives a commercial centre and the services list has Commercial blinds, the card may add glare across the screens of offices and shops on the main street. Never what is in anyone's window today, never a judgement on the street. Not the glass and the sun: the category page owns that.
cards.mechanism: a front window on the pavement with nothing adjustable at it

cards.title: Rooms under the roof and glass extensions
cards.brief: A loft bedroom light from overhead at dawn, a conservatory nobody sits in from late spring until the sun is off it, a kitchen extension with a glass roof that is a greenhouse by midday. The one cause this card makes: glass overhead, which the sun reaches all day long with nothing in the way; the town profile says where lofts have been converted and where the estates were built with conservatories (the pack's section 3: only where the research confirms it). What the work gives, from the trade facts stages: a roof window blind chosen by the window's make and size code, with side rails where the dark matters; conservatory roof blinds measured pane by pane, with a reflective backing against the heat; the fitting planned round safe access to a roof. Said as what it reduces, never a temperature promised. Not a window a ready made blind will not fit: the category page owns that.
cards.mechanism: glass overhead, which the sun reaches all day

cards.title: Blinds and curtains that came with the house
cards.brief: New owners with blinds cut for the last household's use of the room, a corded blind in what is now a child's room, curtains made for a different window, a track whose gliders are long gone. The one cause this card makes: coverings fitted for a previous owner's use of the room (the profile: a new estate where the builder's blinds were a stop gap, an older street where homes change hands with their curtains). What a first visit sorts out, from the trade facts stages: each window measured again rather than assumed, a device added to an older corded blind with its warning labels left on, as what usually applies, curtains relined or shortened where the fabric is good, a blind of a known make repaired where its parts exist. Never a judgement on the previous owner, never a scare about the cords, never 'past saving' as a sale. Not a worn part as a fault: the Blind repairs page owns that.
cards.mechanism: coverings fitted for a previous owner's use of the room

cost.h2: What Affects the Cost of [WORK] in [TOWN]

cards.title: Streets of bays and sash windows
cards.brief: Where the town's older streets were built with bays and deep sash recesses, a bay takes a track bent to its shape or a blind to each face, and a deep recess takes more measuring than a flat uPVC window. Say why that adds time, from the town profile where it gives the housing era (the trade facts price rows: bay faces, custom bending, more units). No figure.

cards.title: Tall windows and roof glass
cards.brief: A stairwell window, a conservatory roof, a roof window over a bed or a landing: the fitting is planned round safe access and takes longer than a window reached from the floor (the trade facts price rows: high access). From the profile where it gives tall period houses, converted lofts or conservatories. No figure.

cards.title: What's behind the plaster on the newer estates
cards.brief: Plasterboard reveals over steel lintels, concrete lintels in post war homes, uPVC frames: each takes its own fixing, and the wall is checked for hidden cables and pipes before any drilling (the trade facts stages and fact rows). Say the business looks before it prices, from [CV: quote_method] only; the era from the profile. No figure.

cards.title: Listed homes and conservation areas
cards.brief: Where the town has listed buildings or conservation areas, an awning or outside shutters can need consent before they go up, and some things cannot be done at all; a blind or curtain inside usually needs nothing. "Usually", never the order's or the area's official name. From the dossier rules only; otherwise a check with the council as something that sometimes applies. No figure.

faq_slots.question: How much does [WORK_LOWER] cost in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Prices only from [CV: price_list]; otherwise the things that push the price up in a town like this (bays and shaped windows, height and access, what the brackets go into) and how the quote is given, from [CV: quote_method] only.

faq_slots.question: How soon can you get to [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: start_time] and [CV: response_time] only. The town is in the area covered; nothing about distance unless [CV: travel_distance] is set.

faq_slots.question: Do you cover [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Yes: the town and the villages around it (code lists them; name none). How the business reaches it from its base only from the client values. Link one page in this town.

faq_slots.question: Do you guarantee your work in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Start with yes, then the terms from [CV: guarantee_years] and [CV: guarantee_scope]. Described, never promised.

faq_slots.question: Are you insured?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for. Never what it pays or who it covers.

faq_slots.question: What happens if something isn't right after the fitting?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the customer does: tell us and we look at it. Then the reasonable care and skill standard every trade works to. No promise to come back free. Never invent a guarantee.

faq_slots.question: What happens when I ask for a quote in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] and the confirmed practices only: what the customer sends, what the business measures and looks at, what comes back. No timescale unless [CV: response_time] is set.

faq_slots.question: Do you work in [TOWN] all year round?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Yes for anything indoors: the trade facts timing cells put blind, curtain and shutter fitting in any month. An awning or anything fixed outside waits for suitable weather, and a conservatory roof or a roof window for safe access on the day. Where the town profile gives the housing (conservatories on the estates, converted lofts), say what it means for the fitting, not for the diary. Nothing about a busy season or booking ahead. No dates.
